body: {"status":"ok","message-type":"work-list","message-version":"1.0.0","message":{"facets":{},"total-results":1327404,"items":[{"DOI":"10.32657\/10220\/47795","title":["Knowledge graph embedding models for automatic commonsense knowledge acquisition"],"author":[{"given":"Mohammad Suliman Alhussien","family":"Ikhlas","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"role":"author","vocabulary":"crossref"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"is-referenced-by-count":0,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.32657\/10220\/47795","type":"dissertation"},{"abstract":"<jats:title>Mesure et enrichissement s\u00e9mantiques des mod\u00e8les \u00e0 base d'embeddings pour la pr\u00e9diction de liens dans les graphes de connaissances<\/jats:title>\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\"fr\">Les mod\u00e8les d'embeddings \u00e0 base de graphes de connaissances ont consid\u00e9rablement gagn\u00e9 en popularit\u00e9 ces derni\u00e8res ann\u00e9es. Ces mod\u00e8les apprennent une repr\u00e9sentation vectorielle des entit\u00e9s et des relations des graphes de connaissances (GCs). Cette th\u00e8se explore sp\u00e9cifiquement le progr\u00e8s de tels mod\u00e8les pour la t\u00e2che de pr\u00e9diction de lien (PL), qui est d'une importance capitale car elle se retrouve dans plusieurs applications telles que les syst\u00e8mes de recommandation. Dans cette th\u00e8se, divers d\u00e9fis li\u00e9s \u00e0 l'utilisation des mod\u00e8les d'embeddings de GCs pour la PL sont identifi\u00e9s : la raret\u00e9 des ressources s\u00e9mantiquement riches, la nature unidimensionnelle des cadres d'\u00e9valuation, et le manque de consid\u00e9rations s\u00e9mantiques dans les approches d'apprentissage automatique. Cette th\u00e8se propose des solutions novatrices \u00e0 ces d\u00e9fis. Premi\u00e8rement, elle contribue au d\u00e9veloppement de ressources s\u00e9mantiquement riches : les jeux de donn\u00e9es principaux pour la pr\u00e9diction de lien sont enrichis en utilisant des informations bas\u00e9es sur des sch\u00e9mas, EducOnto et EduKG sont propos\u00e9s pour surmonter la p\u00e9nurie de ressources dans le domaine \u00e9ducatif, et PyGraft est introduit comme un outil innovant pour g\u00e9n\u00e9rer des ontologies synth\u00e9tiques et des graphes de connaissances. Deuxi\u00e8mement, la th\u00e8se propose une nouvelle m\u00e9trique d'\u00e9valuation orient\u00e9e s\u00e9mantique, Sem@K, offrant une perspective multidimensionnelle sur la performance des mod\u00e8les. Il est important de souligner que les mod\u00e8les populaires sont r\u00e9\u00e9valu\u00e9s en utilisant Sem@K, ce qui r\u00e9v\u00e8le des aspects essentiels et jusqu'alors inexplor\u00e9s de leurs capacit\u00e9s respectives et souligne le besoin de cadres d'\u00e9valuation multidimensionnels. Troisi\u00e8mement, la th\u00e8se se penche sur le d\u00e9veloppement d'approches neuro-symboliques, transcendant les paradigmes traditionnels de l'apprentissage automatique. Ces approches ne d\u00e9montrent pas seulement une meilleure capacit\u00e9 s\u00e9mantique dans leurs pr\u00e9dictions, mais \u00e9tendent \u00e9galement leur utilit\u00e9 \u00e0 diverses applications telles que les syst\u00e8mes de recommandation. En r\u00e9sum\u00e9, le pr\u00e9sent travail ne red\u00e9finit pas seulement l'\u00e9valuation et la fonctionnalit\u00e9 des mod\u00e8les d'embeddings de GCs, mais pr\u00e9pare \u00e9galement le terrain pour des syst\u00e8mes d'intelligence artificielle plus polyvalents et interpr\u00e9tables, soutenant les explorations futures \u00e0 l'intersection de l'apprentissage automatique et du raisonnement symbolique.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.70675\/deffaec5z9178z4a1dzaccez45eda2f2f028","type":"dissertation","is-referenced-by-count":0,"title":["From semantic-aware to semantic-enhanced knowledge graph embedding models for link prediction"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-4682-422X","authenticated-orcid":false,"given":"Nicolas","family":"Hubert","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"id":[{"id":"https:\/\/ror.org\/04vfs2w97","id-type":"ROR","asserted-by":"publisher"}],"name":"Universit\u00e9 de Lorraine"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[null]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.70675\/deffaec5z9178z4a1dzaccez45eda2f2f028"},{"DOI":"10.18653\/v1\/2020.textgraphs-1.1","title":["A survey of embedding models of entities and relationships for knowledge graph completion"],"author":[{"given":"Dat Quoc","family":"Nguyen","sequence":"first","affiliation":[],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2020]]},"container-title":["Proceedings of the Graph-based Methods for Natural Language Processing (TextGraphs)"],"is-referenced-by-count":19,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.18653\/v1\/2020.textgraphs-1.1","type":"proceedings-article"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Large language models (LLMs) have attracted a lot of attention in various fields due to their superior performance, aiming to train hundreds of millions or more parameters on large amounts of text data to understand and generate natural language. As the superior performance of LLMs becomes apparent, they are increasingly being applied to knowledge graph embedding (KGE)-related tasks to improve the processing results. Traditional KGE representation learning methods map entities and relations into a low-dimensional vector space, enabling the triples in the knowledge graph to satisfy a specific scoring function in the vector space. However, based on the powerful language understanding and semantic modeling capabilities of LLMs, which have recently been invoked to varying degrees in different types of KGE-related scenarios such as multi-modal KGE and open KGE according to their task characteristics, researchers are increasingly exploring how to integrate LLMs to enhance knowledge representation, improve generalization to unseen entities or relations, and support reasoning beyond static graph structures. In this paper, we investigate a wide range of approaches for performing LLMs-related tasks in different types of KGE scenarios. To better compare the various approaches, we summarize each KGE scenario in a classification. In the article we also discuss the applications in which the methods are mainly used and suggest several forward-looking directions for the development of this new research Systems"],"is-referenced-by-count":52,"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.1016\/j.knosys.2024.112454","type":"journal-article"},{"abstract":"<jats:title>Abstract<\/jats:title>\n               <jats:p>Recent advances in Knowledge Graphs (KGs) and Knowledge Graph Embedding Models (KGEMs) have led to their adoption in a broad range of fields and applications. The current publishing system in machine learning requires newly introduced KGEMs to achieve state-of-the-art performance, surpassing at least one benchmark in order to be published. Despite this, dozens of novel architectures are published every year, making it challenging for users, even within the field, to deduce the most suitable configuration for a given application. A typical biomedical application of KGEMs is drug\u2013disease prediction in the context of drug discovery, in which a KGEM is trained to predict triples linking drugs and diseases. These predictions can be later tested in clinical trials following extensive experimental validation. However, given the infeasibility of evaluating each of these predictions and that only a minimal number of candidates can be experimentally tested, models that yield higher precision on the top prioritized triples are preferred. In this paper, we apply the concept of ensemble learning on KGEMs for drug discovery to assess whether combining the predictions of several models can lead to an overall improvement in predictive performance. First, we trained and benchmarked 10 KGEMs to predict drug\u2013disease triples on two independent biomedical KGs designed for drug discovery. Following, we applied different ensemble methods that aggregate the predictions of these models by leveraging the distribution or the position of the predicted triple scores. We then demonstrate how the ensemble models can achieve better results than the original KGEMs by benchmarking the precision (i.e., number of true positives prioritized) of their top predictions. Despite the rapid development of KGE models, state-of-the-art approaches have mostly focused on new ways to represent embeddings interaction functions (i.e., scoring functions). In this paper, we argue that the choice of other training components such as the loss function, hyperparameters and negative sampling strategies can also have substantial impact on the model efficiency. This area has been rather neglected by previous works so far and our contribution is towards closing this gap by a thorough analysis of possible choices of training loss functions, hyperparameters and negative sampling techniques.
